correctness.rationale: For every bundle, two initially white leaves can only be forced by their common spoke and permanently prevent that spoke from having a unique white pendant neighbor, so every zero forcing set contains at least \(s-1\) leaves per bundle. The layer of exactly \(m(s-1)\) selected leaves stalls with the center and one leaf per bundle white, proving the extra-vertex lower bound. At minimum size there is exactly one vertex of slack: a center gives the two-step family, an additional pendant saturates exactly one bundle and gives the three-step family, while a spoke leaves every spoke with the center and its omitted leaf simultaneously white and therefore fails. Counting follows independently by omitted-leaf choices. Exhaustive direct verification agrees on \(969{,}903\) candidate minimum subsets across ten parameter pairs and directly checks \(69{,}801\) subsets one below the claimed minimum in manageable cases.

value.rationale: The same-object literature determines the optimal cardinality but leaves the optimal placements unresolved. The classification shows that the one unit of slack above the forced pendant baseline has only two viable structural locations—at the center or as saturation of one pendant bundle—and that these two choices have different propagation times. This yields an exact natural coefficient, an efficient-set census, and a complete boundary description for a standard infinite graph family rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
